answer.rationale: The two degrading metrics are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and the inherited record points directly at that funnel: memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (cutting required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift). Those are the two I want the archived source records for, because they are the memories I would actually be acting on — I want to see effect sizes, segment scope, and whether the 'durable' claim in memory_31 was measured beyond week one before I commit the single slot to them. The competitor's entry pricing creates real pull toward promotional_pricing, and that is exactly the trap: memory_73 records strong acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention drop, with an explicit instruction not to generalize it as a growth strategy. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching an aggressive price move would buy accounts that churn, so I am not spending the slot there even though it is the most direct answer to the competitive event. Referral incentive (memory_57) is clean but addresses established customers, not the funnel that is actually eroding. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but a different segment and slower to read. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the closest runner-up and would be my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding records; I prefer simplification because it addresses the earlier funnel stage where both declines originate rather than compensating downstream. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the prior evidence is supportive but was measured in an earlier competitive environment, and a 6%/4% decline may have causes the archive did not test. Downstream value risk to flag: removing signup fields improves activation metrics while potentially degrading lead qualification and routing data, which is precisely how memory_44's enterprise demo-request advantage could be quietly eroded — so I will instrument for qualified-pipeline quality and 30-day retention, not just activation counts, and I will record the retention caveat rather than letting a clean activation number overwrite it.
